decision.summary: Seed 1201 passes the first moving-band screen: 38 bodies and all three families at 3,000, continuing births and deaths, low ceiling occupancy, and concrete spatial differences from uniform. Stop after this seed; replication is the next proposed slice.

visualComparisons.observation: Uniform has separated clusters across the left edge, upper middle and lower right. Moving-band has a much denser upper-middle branching group and a near-continuous central vertical arrangement, with a broad empty region on the right. This concerns occupied bodies, not the outline.
Uniform has occupied groups spread across the left-middle, upper-right and right-middle. Moving-band concentrates a tall chain of occupied groups in the right half and leaves a broad left-side gap.

Uniform retains occupied clusters across both halves, including a large mint arrangement in the upper-right. Moving-band has gold groups near the upper-right edge and dense purple branches in the lower-right, with a much broader central-left gap.

lateWithinMoving.observation: The moving worlds central-right mint chain becomes a gap with only sparse mint bodies. Purple branches consolidate farther right and gold bodies redistribute along the upper-right edge. Occupied locations and gaps change beyond family color replacement.

numericalGate.note: Descriptive trajectory novelty screen only; visual judgment is manual. No claim of tracking, adaptation, fitness improvement, or superiority.

decision.reason: All frozen numerical and visual criteria pass. This is a varied different trajectory under the whole band design, not proof of tracking, adaptation or superiority.
